label: early 3-gram q, {e,q,w,k,a}, {c,d,y,2,f,w,p,v} in the original phase
explanation: A sparse early-sequence trigram detector. 94% of activation mass is in the original phase, almost all at t=2-4 (t=2: 49%, t=3: 36%). It never fires at t=0 or t=1. The strongest cue is q two steps back (prev2_tok=q holds 78% of mass, 29x lift). The previous token is usually e, q, w, k or a, and the current token is usually c, d, y, 2, f, w, p or v. The strongest examples begin p q {e,q,w} X; a leading p (first_tok=p, 3.9x) and a first-time token (in_first) push activation up. Below the top, the feature acts like a graded sum over these tokens rather than a strict conjunction. Many weaker activations come from partial matches, such as a or e in place of q, or a different third token (e, 1, a, u). Many exact matches with q at position 2 (t=4) stay silent. It is almost silent at the delimiter and in the copy phase; the only copy-phase activity is a small amount (~6% of mass) at recall_idx 1 and at the last few steps of L=9 sequences. The predicate covers only about half the mass, so the explanation is incomplete.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: prev2_tok=q (+5.47), prev_tok=w (+4.64), prev_tok=e (+4.60), prev_tok=q (+4.33), phase=2 & in_tok=i (+3.65), prev_tok=k (+3.48). Lower it: correct=1 (-6.17), recall_idx=4 (-5.49), recall_idx=3 (-3.10), prev3_tok=<DEL> (-3.10).
